questions.q: What happens with manual (standard) provisioned throughput when traffic exceeds the configured RU/s?
options: Requests get throttled with a 429 response until the next second's RU budget resets
Cosmos DB automatically raises the RU/s without any billing change
The container is automatically deleted
Excess requests are queued indefinitely with no error
questions.explain: Manual throughput is a hard ceiling — exceeding it results in throttled (429) requests, not automatic scaling.

questions.q: How does autoscale throughput actually scale?
options: Automatically and near-instantly between a floor of 10% of the configured maximum and that maximum, based on real-time usage
It scales linearly by a fixed percentage every 24 hours
It requires a manual approval step before each scale event
It only scales upward and never back down
questions.explain: Autoscale's floor is always 10% of the configured max RU/s, and the system moves between floor and ceiling automatically based on demand.

options: Based on the highest RU/s the system actually scaled to during each hour, not the configured maximum
Always at the full configured maximum, every hour, regardless of usage
A flat monthly fee unrelated to RU/s consumption
Billing is identical to manual throughput in every case
questions.explain: A quiet hour is billed near the floor even with a high ceiling configured — this is what makes autoscale attractive for variable workloads.

questions.q: Per this lesson, which workload is the better fit for manual throughput rather than autoscale?
options: Steady, predictable, well-understood traffic that can be right-sized confidently
A dev/test environment with unpredictable, spiky traffic
A brand-new application with no established traffic pattern
A workload with occasional flash-sale-style spikes
questions.explain: Manual throughput is the right fit when usage is steady and well-understood, since it typically costs less than autoscale's premium.

questions.q: Besides the throughput model, what other real cost levers does this lesson mention?
options: Tuning the indexing policy to exclude unqueried paths, choosing a well-distributed partition key, and preferring point reads over cross-partition queries
Disabling the change feed entirely
Switching every workload to the Cassandra API
There are no other real cost levers besides throughput model choice
questions.explain: These are the additional cost optimization levers the lesson connects back to earlier chapter concepts (indexing, partitioning, query patterns).
